title: Boss: where did my data go?
summary: Model mounts, addresses and persistence well enough to answer the questions teammates ask after an incident.

steps.title: Post-incident questions
steps.body: Someone ran `docker rm` on the wrong thing, a dashboard cannot reach the database, and nobody is sure which files survived. Build tools that answer these precisely.

steps.title: Read --mount
prompt: Write `string ParseMount(string spec)` for the long `--mount` syntax: comma-separated `key=value` pairs, plus the bare flag `readonly` (or `ro`).
- `type` is `volume` (default), `bind` or `tmpfs`
- the source is `source` or `src`; the target is `target`, `dst` or `destination`
Output, with ` (read-only)` appended when the flag is present:
| type | output |
| volume with a source | `named volume SOURCE -> TARGET` |
| volume without a source | `anonymous volume -> TARGET` |
| bind | `bind mount SOURCE -> TARGET` |
| tmpfs | `tmpfs -> TARGET` |
solution: else if (key == "target" || key == "dst" || key == "destination") target = value;

steps.title: Which address?
prompt: Write `string Address(string from, string target, int containerPort, Dictionary<string, string> published, Dictionary<string, string> networkOf)`.
- `from` is `host` or a container name; `target` is a container name.
- `published[c]` holds container c's `-p` mappings as `"hostPort:containerPort"`, comma-separated (`"8080:8080,8443:8443"`); a container with nothing published is missing from the dictionary.
- `networkOf[c]` is the one user-defined network container c is on.
From `host`: if `target` publishes `containerPort`, return `localhost:HOSTPORT`, otherwise `not reachable: port CONTAINERPORT is not published`.
From a container: if both are on the same network, return `TARGET:CONTAINERPORT`, otherwise `not reachable: no shared network`.
starter: string Address(string from, string target, int containerPort, Dictionary<string, string> published, Dictionary<string, string> networkOf)
solution: string Address(string from, string target, int containerPort, Dictionary<string, string> published, Dictionary<string, string> networkOf)
return $"not reachable: port {containerPort} is not published";
return networkOf[from] == networkOf[target] ? $"{target}:{containerPort}" : "not reachable: no shared network";
template: Dojo.Eq("host -> api", "not reachable: port 8080 is not published", Address("host", "api", 8080, dojoPub, dojoNet));
Dojo.Eq("host -> db wrong port", "not reachable: port 5433 is not published", Address("host", "db", 5433, dojoPub, dojoNet));
Dojo.Eq("grafana -> db", "not reachable: no shared network", Address("grafana", "db", 5432, dojoPub, dojoNet));

steps.title: What survives docker rm?
prompt: A container was run with some mounts and wrote some files; then someone ran `docker rm` on it (with `-v` if `withV` is true). Write `List<string> AfterRm(List<string> mounts, List<string> files, bool withV)`.

`mounts` are `-v` style values: `name:/target` (named volume), `./x:/target` or `/x:/target` (bind mount; source starts with `/` `.` or `~`), `/target` alone (anonymous volume), or `tmpfs:/target` (tmpfs). For each file, find the mount whose target is the **longest** match (the file equals the target or is under `target/`), and output one line:
| where | line |
| no mount | `PATH: lost (container writable layer)` |
| named volume | `PATH: kept (named volume NAME)` |
| bind mount | `PATH: kept (host folder SOURCE)` |
| anonymous volume | `PATH: lost (anonymous volume removed by -v)` when `withV`, else `PATH: kept (anonymous volume, now orphaned)` |
| tmpfs | `PATH: lost (tmpfs lives in memory)` |
starter: List<string> AfterRm(List<string> mounts, List<string> files, bool withV)
solution: List<string> AfterRm(List<string> mounts, List<string> files, bool withV)
if (under && target.Length > bestTarget.Length) { best = m; bestTarget = target; }
else if (!best.Contains(':')) where = withV ? "lost (anonymous volume removed by -v)" : "kept (anonymous volume, now orphaned)";
else if (source.StartsWith("/") || source.StartsWith(".") || source.StartsWith("~")) where = $"kept (host folder {source})";
template: Dojo.Eq("with -v the anonymous volume goes", new List<string> { "/app/cache/x: lost (anonymous volume removed by -v)", "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_hba.conf: kept (named volume pgdata)" },

Dojo.Eq("longest target wins; prefix is not enough", new List<string> { "/app/data/keep/a: kept (named volume keep)", "/app/data/b: kept (host folder /srv/data)", "/app/database/c: lost (container writable layer)" },
hints: The target is everything after the first `:`, or the whole value when there is no colon.
`/app/database` must not match the target `/app/data`: compare with `target + "/"`.
Remember the longest matching target, then classify only that mount.
